title: Oriented nearby cycles, base-change comparison and Psi-good pairs
statement:
Let $f:T\to B$ be a morphism of schemes and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Use their small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with geometric morphisms in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Define the vanishing topos
$$V_f=T_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}B_{\mathrm{Et}}$$
to be the left oriented product of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] for $f:T_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $\operatorname{id}:B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$, i.e. the topos of sheaves on the site of triples $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ there, with $\mathcal C_1=T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal D=B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $f^{-1}V=V\times_BT$: it has projections $p_1:V_f\to T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $p_2:V_f\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and a $2$-morphism $p_2\Rightarrow fp_1$, universal for this data by that lemma (equivalently, morphisms from any topos $\mathcal E$ to $V_f$ are pairs $a:\mathcal E\to T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $b:\mathcal E\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with a $2$-morphism $b\Rightarrow fa$). Here a $2$-morphism is a natural transformation of geometric morphisms, in the orientation displayed. The morphism $\psi_f:T_{\mathrm{Et}}\to V_f$ corresponds to $(1_T,f,1_f)$. With constant coefficient sheaves put
$$D(V_f,\Lambda)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{V_f})),\qquad R\Psi_f=R\psi_{f,*}.$$
The module and derived categories are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; total right derived direct image is computed on K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Derived tensor on any of these ringed topoi is computed on K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. $D^b$ means cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval.

A commutative square $(h,g):f'\to f$ induces $v:V_{f'}\to V_f$. Define its ordinary comparison $v^*R\Psi_fL\to R\Psi_{f'}h^*L$ to be the adjunction mate of the inverse-image square. The pair $(f,L)$ is called $\Psi$-good if this map is an isomorphism for every Cartesian square obtained by an arbitrary scheme morphism $g:B'\to B$. The lax tensor map for $R\Psi_f$ is adjoint to the tensor of the two counits $\psi_f^*R\Psi_fL\to L$.

For two morphisms $f_i:T_i\to B$, put $T=T_1\times_BT_2$, let $f:T\to B$ be the structure map, let $q_i:T\to T_i$ be the projections and $v_i:V_f\to V_{f_i}$ the induced maps. On $T$ write $L_1\boxtimes_B^LL_2=q_1^*L_1\otimes_\Lambda^Lq_2^*L_2$; on $V_f$ write $P_1\boxtimes^LP_2=v_1^*P_1\otimes_\Lambda^Lv_2^*P_2$. Define the oriented Kunneth comparison as the ordinary comparisons for $q_1,q_2$, followed by the lax tensor map of $R\Psi_f$.

source.place: Expose XI, Definition 1.7, universal property 1.4 and 4.1--4.3, pp. 171--185; Psi-goodness and comparison notation: Illusie, Around the Thom--Sebastiani theorem, 1.4--1.5 (local PDF WANTED).
